key_insight: A three-agent framework connects high-level network intents to runtime control by jointly adapting intent specifications and controller policies.
engineering_relevance: The approach could help autonomous mobile networks translate service requirements into adaptive radio resource management actions.
method: A language-model interpreter translates and refines intents into machine-readable optimization templates.
A Bayesian optimizer adapts controller policies to intent specifications.
A multi-objective reinforcement learning controller makes fast runtime decisions.
evidence_signal: A radio resource management case study for differentiated connectivity demonstrates adaptation to service requirements and changing network conditions, although the abstract reports no quantitative metrics.
watch_item: Deployment requires validating intent translation and policy adaptation against network safety constraints and runtime latency budgets.
paper_title: Agentic AI for Intent Management and Control in Autonomous Communication Networks
